---
title: "How to Contribute"
toc: false
---

This documentation is designed to be easy to review and improve.

If you are a clinician or reviewer, you can contribute without installing any tools.

## Option 1: Report an issue (recommended for feedback)

On any page, use the **Issue** / **Report an issue** link.

- This opens a GitHub Issue where you can describe the change you want.
- This is best for requests, questions, or feedback that needs discussion.

## Option 2: Suggest a direct edit in the browser

On any page, use the **Edit** link.

This will open the corresponding source file (a `.qmd` file) on GitHub.

Typical flow:

1. Click **Edit**.
2. Make a small change (typo fix, wording clarification, etc.).
3. GitHub will prompt you to create a **new branch** and open a **Pull Request (PR)**.
4. Submit the PR.

A maintainer will review the PR and merge it when approved.

## Option 3: Edit locally (for larger changes)

If you are comfortable with developer tools:

1. Clone the repository.
2. Edit `.qmd` files.
3. Preview locally with `quarto preview`.
4. Open a PR.

## What happens after you contribute

- Proposed changes are reviewed via Pull Requests.
- The public website is published from version tags (e.g. `v0.2.0`) rather than every merge.

## Tips for making good edits

- Keep changes small and focused.
- Prefer plain language.
- For IFU/safety content: keep wording unambiguous and consistent.

## Style snippets

### Figure with a standard caption

```markdown
![](images/example.png){fig-alt="Example image" fig-cap="Figure: Example caption."}
```

### Figure with a margin note (recommended for short callouts)

Use a margin note when you want a small explanation beside the figure (e.g., what to look for).

```markdown
![](images/example.png){fig-alt="Example image" fig-cap="Figure: Example caption."}

::: {.column-margin}
Key point: Describe what to look for in the image.
:::
```
